log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 59% BRING: dragapult, 28% BRING: garchomp, 4% BRING: gholdengo
Pick 2: 70% BRING: garchomp, 23% BRING: gholdengo, 3% BRING: greninja
Pick 3: 87% BRING: gholdengo, 6% BRING: scizor, 6% BRING: greninja

Incineroar leads to use Intimidate and Fake Out against the physical threats. Kingambit handles Greninja and Palafin, and Gholdengo covers the Dragapult and Scizor matchups with strong special coverage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick 3 from my team against their dragapult/garchomp/gholdengo/scizor/greninja/palafin squad. Weighing Incineroar for intimidate and pivot support, and checking Kingambit's matchup since its Dark/Steel typing resists dragon but leaves it exposed to fire, fighting, and ground.

Archaludon's Steel/Dragon typing covers their dragons well despite ground/fire/fighting weaknesses, while Gholdengo pressures scizor and palafin with special attacks and hits Dragapult's ghost typing super-effectively. I'll settle on Incineroar, Kingambit, and Gholdengo, leading with Incineroar.

decisions.thought: 38% MOVE: suckerpunch, 20% MOVE: shadowball, 18% SWITCH: garchomp

Fake Out does nothing to Dragapult because it's Ghost-type, and Flare Blitz is resisted by Dragon. Parting Shot lowers Dragapult's Attack and Sp. Atk while pivoting Incineroar out before Dragapult, which is much faster, can punish it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since Dragapult is Ghost-type, Fake Out's Normal-type attack has no effect on it, making that move useless here, and Flare Blitz would only be resisted damage against the Dragon typing.

Parting Shot could further cripple Dragapult's Atk and SpA while letting me pivot into Kingambit or Gholdengo, though I need to weigh typing matchups—Dragapult's Ghost STAB hits Kingambit hard, while its Dragon Darts aren't resisted by either switch-in. Protect is a safer scouting option since Incineroar is slower and vulnerable to Dragapult's coverage moves either way.

decisions.thought: Dragapult outspeeds Incineroar, but Parting Shot already cut its Attack and Special Attack. Kingambit resists Dark, so Sucker Punch does little to it, and its Dark attacks are super effective against Dragapult's Ghost typing. Gholdengo would take a super-effective Sucker Punch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing switching to Kingambit or Gholdengo against the weakened Dragapult, checking type matchups since Dark and Ghost moves trade super-effective hits against each other, so Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing is risky against Dragapult's Ghost STAB.

Kingambit looks safer overall since it resists Dark (Sucker Punch) and only takes neutral damage from Dragon, while Gholdengo's Ghost typing is doubly weak to both Dark and Ghost attacks. With Dragapult's attack dropped, Kingambit seems like the better switch to pressure it with Kowtow Cleave or Iron Head.

decisions.thought: 59% MOVE: suckerpunch, 32% SWITCH: garchomp, 9% SWITCH: gholdengo

Dragapult is already at -2 Attack and -1 Special Attack, so its Sucker Punch hits much weaker. Kowtow Cleave is a super-effective Dark move with STAB and Black Glasses, and it never misses, so it should knock Dragapult out. Kingambit's 177 HP can survive Dragapult's reduced attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking type effectiveness: Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave is Dark-type, which hits Dragapult's Ghost typing for super effective damage since Dragon/Ghost isn't resistant to Dark.

Running the damage math with Kingambit's 205 attack, STAB, Black Glasses boost, and the 2x super effective multiplier against Dragapult's defense range, it comes out to a clean KO regardless of whether Dragapult invested in defense. The key risk is Dragapult's Sucker Punch, which would only connect if Kingambit is the one attacking that turn—so speed order matters, but Kowtow Cleave's guaranteed accuracy makes it the safest choice either way.

decisions.thought: 73% SWITCH: garchomp, 27% SWITCH: gholdengo
83% MOVE: earthquake, 5% MOVE: dracometeor, 5% MOVE: swordsdance

Garchomp is likely faster than Kingambit, so it will hit first, but Kingambit at 168/177 should survive a single hit. Kowtow Cleave is a reliable, non-accuracy-checking Dark attack that hits Garchomp neutrally for heavy damage. Swords Dance gives Garchomp a free turn to attack, and switching only brings in another Ground-weak Pokémon.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Checking type matchups: Garchomp's Ground hits Kingambit's Steel typing for 2x damage, while Kingambit's Iron Head is only neutral against Garchomp's Dragon/Ground typing, giving Garchomp the advantage here.

Garchomp also likely outspeeds Kingambit, so it strikes first with Earthquake, and Kowtow Cleave wouldn't be enough to knock it out in return. I'm also weighing whether switching to Gholdengo or Incineroar is better, but both are also weak to Ground-type attacks, so none of these options cleanly beats Garchomp.

Incineroar also takes the 2x EQ hit but has decent bulk and should survive, setting up another Intimidate and leaving Garchomp at -1 while keeping Flare Blitz in reserve. Weighing that against just attacking now with Kowtow Cleave, risking Garchomp's EQ KO on Kingambit versus trading the safer intimidate switch.

decisions.thought: Kingambit fainted to Earthquake, so I must switch. Gholdengo is Steel, which takes double damage from Garchomp's Earthquake, and Life Orb makes that worse. Incineroar takes only neutral damage from Earthquake, and its Intimidate triggers again on entry to cut Garchomp's Attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Kingambit down, I need to check matchups against Garchomp's Earthquake - Incineroar as Fire/Dark takes neutral damage from Ground, so that's a safer switch than something weak to it.

Gholdengo being Steel/Ghost is actually weak to Ground (2x), so that's risky against Life Orb Garchomp. Incineroar also brings Intimidate to cut Garchomp's attack, making it the clearly better switch-in here.

decisions.thought: 78% MOVE: earthquake, 8% MOVE: swordsdance, 6% SWITCH: gholdengo

Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar and its Earthquake is super effective on both Incineroar and Gholdengo. Parting Shot drops its Attack to -2, which weakens the next Earthquake, and pivots Incineroar out with Sitrus Berry intact. Gholdengo can then come in and take the hit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since Fake Out isn't legal this turn, I'm weighing Flare Blitz against Garchomp, which is only half-effective since Fire resists Dragon, versus Garchomp's Earthquake hitting Incineroar neutrally.

Gholdengo is also on the bench and would be doubly weak to Earthquake as Steel-type, so switching in to it doesn't solve the ground weakness. Parting Shot could drop Garchomp's attack further while pivoting to Gholdengo, but Gholdengo still eats a 2x Earthquake, though it resists Electric-immune Garchomp back with Shadow Ball or Make It Rain doing neutral damage.

Protect is also tempting—it costs nothing this turn, lets Incineroar stall the Earthquake, and sets up Parting Shot next turn once the opponent's move is revealed, since Garchomp's Life Orb recoil only applies when it actually lands a hit.

Weighing it out, Parting Shot wins: it drops Garchomp further to -2 Attack, weakens future Earthquake damage significantly, and pivots Incineroar out safely into Gholdengo while preserving its Sitrus Berry for later. I'll go with Parting Shot.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is at 65 HP, slower than Garchomp, and its only legal option is switching to Gholdengo. Gholdengo is the sole legal action, so I must switch.
56% MOVE: earthquake, 26% MOVE: swordsdance, 8% MOVE: stealthrock

Garchomp is at 80% and Thunderbolt does nothing to it. Make It Rain's 120 power plus STAB and Life Orb should likely knock it out, even though it drops Gholdengo's Sp. Atk. Shadow Ball is a safer hit but leaves Garchomp alive.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking type matchups against Garchomp: Thunderbolt is immune since it's Dragon/Ground, Shadow Ball hits neutrally, and I'm working out whether Steel-type moves like Make It Rain are resisted by Dragon.

Shadow Ball seems like the safer choice given Make It Rain's severe SpA drop, so I'm estimating damage output — with Gholdengo's 203 SpA and Life Orb boost, Shadow Ball's STAB-less 80 power should still deal roughly 120 damage after modifiers, which could put a serious dent in Garchomp's remaining HP.

The SpA drop from Make It Rain matters less since this is likely the deciding move anyway, and the remaining threats can be handled afterward. I'll go with Make It Rain.

decisions.thought: 78% MOVE: earthquake, 8% SWITCH: gholdengo, 6% MOVE: swordsdance

Garchomp is at 70% and Gholdengo has only 31 HP, so Gholdengo likely dies to Earthquake if it stays in without a KO. Thunderbolt is immune to Dragon/Ground, and Make It Rain would cost 2 Sp. Atk. Shadow Ball with STAB and Life Orb should deal roughly 130 damage, close to Garchomp's remaining HP, so it is the best attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo's down to 31/164 HP, and Garchomp is at 70% with Life Orb, carrying -2 attack and -1 special attack. Earthquake is physical so the attack drop hurts its damage, but Ground still hits Gholdengo's Steel typing for super effective damage.

I'm weighing Shadow Ball, which deals roughly 130 damage against Garchomp's remaining HP pool — close enough that it's uncertain whether it kills outright. Make It Rain drops its own special attack further, which seems counterproductive now, and Thunderbolt is useless since Garchomp's Ground typing grants Electric immunity.

Garchomp's EQ at -2 attack would likely still knock out Gholdengo's 31 HP, so switching to Incineroar risks triggering Intimidate again but exposes it to a big hit. Shadow Ball still looks like the strongest option here, so I'll go with that.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo has fainted, so the only legal action is switching to Incineroar. I must choose that switch.
77% MOVE: earthquake, 9% SWITCH: gholdengo, 7% MOVE: swordsdance

Incineroar is our last Pokémon, so Parting Shot has no switch-in and Fake Out is not usable after turn one. Garchomp is faster and sits at -3 Attack, so it probably won't KO Incineroar with Earthquake this turn. Flare Blitz deals the most damage available now, even at half effectiveness.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's HP is low and Garchomp has -3 Attack from Life Orb boosts, so I should question whether Fake Out is actually usable here since it's not the first turn—the legality listing might be wrong, so I'll steer clear of it. With Garchomp's attack so heavily lowered, Earthquake's damage output would be significantly reduced too.

Flare Blitz is resisted since Fire is weak against Dragon, so it won't come close to KOing Garchomp at 60% HP. Working through the math, Garchomp's weakened Earthquake probably deals somewhere in the 40-60% range to Incineroar, leaving it in a precarious spot where I need to decide whether to attack, protect, or pivot out with something like Parting Shot to bring in a healthier teammate.

Protect could stall one turn, costing Garchomp's LO recoil and keeping Incineroar safe from that hit, but Garchomp's attack stays lowered and its follow-up Flare Blitz still wouldn't secure the KO even after Sitrus Berry activates.

Comparing attacking now instead: if Incineroar is faster and uses Flare Blitz first, it chips Garchomp down to roughly a third of its health, but then Garchomp's Earthquake next turn leaves Incineroar at a sliver of HP, and if Garchomp moves first instead, EQ leaves Incineroar barely alive before Flare Blitz's recoil might finish it off anyway. Protect still looks like the safer play to avoid losing Incineroar outright.

Either path seems rough for Incineroar against Garchomp — the exact damage rolls are uncertain, and Parting Shot likely fails since there's no bench Pokemon to switch into, meaning the move would just whiff.

I'll just commit to Flare Blitz for maximum damage now rather than risking Protect or a stat-drop move that might not even function.
